data.title: IRYS crypto jumps nearly 580% as traders betting against it lose $21M
data.description:
Irys [IRYS] surged nearly 580% over 24 hours on October 23, reaching around $0.144. A look at its daily chart showed that it recorded a session high near the $0.157 price area before it eased toward $0.142.

The rally coincided with heavy losses for traders betting on a price decline. Data showed that there were around $21.4 million in short liquidations, but the available data does not show what started the surge or how much forced buying contributed.

The rally accelerated well beyond four cents

IRYS began its daily session at around $0.0206. At the time of this writing, it was trading at almost 7x that level.

A look at the chart shows how the move developed. An initially gradual rise gathered pace after it passed the $0.04 price level, and a more positive move followed, taking the price toward $0.13.

It saw a brief pullback that interrupted that climb before buyers were then able to push the price higher again.

At the time of this writing, the daily chart showed a gain of roughly 592% with trading still ongoing.

Bets against IRYS took most of the liquidation losses

CoinMarketCap data showed around $24.2 million in total liquidations over 24 hours. Around $21.4 million came from shorts, compared with roughly $2.8 million from positions betting on higher prices.

Liquidations happen when an exchange forcibly closes a leveraged trade because the trader can no longer cover its losses.

Closing a short can involve buying back the asset or contract, potentially adding to upward pressure. But these totals cannot show how much of IRYS’s rally came from that process.

The data showed that outstanding futures positions also reached about $1.22 billion. That figure does not only mean that fresh cash is entering; the sharp price it saw raises the value.

What can the chart tell us now?

The session high near $0.157 provides an immediate reference for another advance. Below the latest price, the intraday pause around the $0.115–$0.13 price area offers an area to watch if selling returns, and sellers decide they want to take gains.

But that pause seen on the chart is too recent to call dependable support. But if it holds there through repeated pullbacks, it would mean that buyers are accepting the higher prices.

What is being seen is an interesting repricing and active trading, but where IRYS will settle once the initial surge slows remains to be seen.

Final Summary

  • IRYS gained nearly 580% over 24 hours, moving far beyond the brief’s earlier $0.04 level.
  • Short liquidations reached around $21.4 million, but the rally’s initial trigger is not known yet.

data.title: XLM price edges higher, but Stellar’s October slide is proving hard to reverse
data.description:
Stellar [XLM] recovered slightly on October 23 after it saw a 4.57% decline the previous day. It was near $0.177 at the time of this writing, having briefly reached $0.179 earlier in the session.

The bounce has helped with its recovery, but it has only recovered a small part of what it lost. With it still below the levels it reached during its latest recovery attempt, buyers have more work to do before October’s negative trend can begin to change direction.

A promising rebound has already faded once

Earlier this week, XLM climbed from around $0.175 toward $0.187. That recovery gave traders some breathing room after several weeks of losses it saw.

But by October 22, the price had fallen back toward the $0.175 price area, taking away much of the advance. The small improvement it saw on Friday leaves its price close to where that rebound started.

The four-hour chart shows the difficulty even more clearly when observed. Throughout October, successive recoveries have generally stopped at lower prices. Buyers have managed to interrupt the decline, but they have not been able to build on those gains.

The daily chart also shows how much September’s strength has faded. XLM traded above $0.23 late that month before slipping below $0.18 in October.

What would make this bounce more convincing?

The first improvement would be if it returns above the $0.179–$0.181 price area, followed by XLM then being able to hold that level as it tries to change the trend into a positive one.

That would put the price above its nearest short-term averages, and it will show that buyers are gaining some control.

But the harder test lies around the $0.184–$0.187 price area, because that was where the latest rebound ran out of steam. Moving through that area would interrupt the pattern of recoveries ending at lower prices.

Even then, a wider turnaround would require more progress. The daily chart’s longer-term averages remain overhead, clustered around the $0.188–$0.192 price area.

The recent lows still matter

For now, the $0.174–$0.175 price range looks like the area that buyers need to defend. This is because XLM has visited this range repeatedly in recent sessions.

If the price settles below it and it’s not able to recover, the recent lows around the $0.171–$0.172 price area become an area to watch.

If the price falls briefly below the support area, it’s fine, but if it continues to trade below it, it means decline has set in. Until either buyers reclaim higher ground or those lows give way, it will not be able to complete its recovery from its October decline.

Final Summary

XLM’s modest bounce has recovered only a small portion of its latest decline.

Holding $0.174–$0.175 and recovering $0.181 would improve the immediate outlook.

data.title: Akedo crypto rallies 59% after $62M unlock – What’s driving AKE?
data.description:
Akedo [AKE] unlocked $62 million worth of tokens two days ago, equivalent to 9% of its circulating supply. During the past two unlocks, the altcoin dropped 22% and 49% in the following week.

This time, the market behaved differently. Although it fell to $0.021, it bounced back shortly after, flipped $0.03, and rose to $0.036.

As of this writing, AKE was trading around $0.035, up 59% on the daily charts. The price hike led to a Daily Turnover of $16 million, suggesting increased trading activity during the rally.

Is Akedo’s rally leverage-driven?

Akedo‘s recent rally has captured market participants’ attention, prompting questions about what’s driving it. Professor On-Chain noted that the recent hike was mostly leverage-driven, with Futures volume outpacing Spot volume by 93x.

A look at the derivatives market offers further insight into this claim. For starters, Akedo’s Futures Inflow rose to $215 million, while outflows fell to $207 million.

As a result, Futures Netflow rose 188% to $7.7 million. Additionally, the altcoin’s Open Interest (OI) surged 90.5% to $101 million, while derivatives volume rose 81% to $608 million.

The rising OI and volume indicated increased market participation as traders opened new positions. Meanwhile, the overall Long-Short Ratio rose to 1.03 as of writing, but the ratios on OKX and Binance remained below 1.

The overall ratio suggests a slight tilt towards long positions, while the ratios on OKX and Binance point to more short positions. This suggests mixed sentiment across exchanges.

Spot buyers are stepping in

Besides high leverage, Spot buyers are also chasing the rally. Coinalyze data showed that spot buy volume rose to 12.27 million, compared with 11.7 million in sell volume.

As a result, the Buy-Sell Delta turned positive, rising to 479k, suggesting that buying activity exceeded selling activity. On top of that, Spot Netflow also fell into negative territory again. At press time, Netflow was around -$220k.

A negative Netflow indicates that more assets are leaving exchanges than entering them, which may be consistent with accumulation but does not, on its own, confirm aggressive spot buying.

Can AKE hold the upside momentum?

Akedo is currently having strong bullish momentum. In fact, the altcoin’s Relative Strength Index (RSI) made a bullish crossover and rose to 57 at press time. At these levels, the indicator moved further into bullish territory, reflecting improving momentum.

Often, a rising RSI can accompany further gains. Therefore, if buying pressure holds across the market, traders could see Akedo extend its recovery and flip $0.04.

However, higher leverage poses a risk of larger losses and increased liquidations. If speculation fades, we could see another drop towards $0.021.

Final summary

  • Akedo surged 59%, rebounded from a post-unlock slip, flipped $0.03, and rose to $0.036.
  • AKE rallied, driven by strong speculative demand, with futures volume outpacing spot volume by 93x.

data.title: ICP crypto faces fresh pressure – Why DFINITY accuses NEAR of IP theft
data.description:
Dominic Williams, founder of DFINITY, claims that Near Protocol stole its intellectual property (IP) behind its cross-chain stack, NEAR Intents. DFINITY is the developer of the Internet Computer (ICP) blockchain.

Williams labelled Near’s cross-chain execution as a ‘fake decentralization’ 

The NEAR Intents saga just got much more crazy on further investigation. Much is missing from Intents, but key enabling component turns out to be stolen proprietary DFINITY tech. I’m stunned.

William added that Near Protocol used a former DFINITY employee they fired in 2021. According to him, the ex-employee helped Near Protocol develop its cross-chain NEAR Intents, warning of potential “legal implications.’ 

NEAR Intents uses Chain Abstraction (powered by our proprietary tech) to custody assets on different chains, and then Intents basically just uses a market maker paid by them to swap them across chains according to people’s wishes.

DFINITY and Internet Computer claimed that the IP theft harmed them financially. In fact, William said that even ICP crypto holders have been impacted by alleged NEAR Intent theft. However, he didn’t mention any pending lawsuit, but noted that “something has to be worked out.”

NEAR Intents’ response to Internet Computer claims

As of writing, Illia Polosukhin, founder of Near Protocol, had not responded to the allegations. However, Alex Shevchenko, an executive at Near Protocol, responded with a sarcastic post, indirectly urging his followers to short the ICP token. 

It’s unclear whether DFINITY will escalate the alleged IP theft to court. That said, NEAR Intents has seen more traction than Internet Computer. The cross-chain hit a record $5 billion volume in September with over $8 million in cumulative revenue. 

On the other hand, Internet Computer has seen a sustained drop in network activity. Its total value locked (TVL) has declined from $200 million to about $4 million. The liquidity has also decreased to $4 million from $7 million. 

Impact on ICP crypto

Some community members claimed that the allegations were mere FUD (fear, uncertainty, and disinformation). Critics warned that the FUD would backfire and impact ICP market sentiment. 

Sentiment analysis showed users were neutral on the altcoin as of writing. This was down from its ‘greed’ level of 68 seen on Thursday and last month. On the price charts, ICP dipped 6%, which coincided with a broader market decline. 

Final Summary

  • DFINITY founder claimed that NEAR Intents stole its proprietary tech, financially harming the Internet Computer and ICP token holders.
  • The founder warned of ‘legal implications’ but did not clarify whether it will sue Near Protocol.

data.title: From Alpenglow to Quantumglow – Inside Solana’s post-quantum plan
data.description:
After achieving a massive 85x faster transaction finality via the Alpenglow upgrade, Solana [SOL] is now pitching its quantum upgrade plan. 

On the 22nd of October, Solana and Anza, the software company building some of its core infrastructure, proposed an adaptation of Alpenglow to secure the chain against quantum computer threats. But no dedicated timeline or deadline has been issued yet. 

Post-Alpenglow: Solana quantum plan

The proposal seeks to upgrade Alpenglow signatures, which are currently quantum-vulnerable. At the consensus layer, Solana validators use the heavy and slow BLS (Boneh-Lynn-Shacham) signatures.

For token swaps and transfers between wallets and apps such as Phantom, the faster ED25519 signatures are used. Both signature schemes rely on elliptic curve cryptography, which quantum computers can break. 

Quantumglow seeks to replace BLS with hash-based signatures for validators and ED25519 with Falcon signing. Dilithium and Falcon are among the most widely used quantum-proof signatures. 

For Solana, Quantumglow would still allow the chain to get its post-quantum security while retaining its 0.15-second transaction finality. However, Anza and Solana have not committed to any timeline or deadline for the upgrade. 

Still, this is an incredible update that Alpenglow can be adapted to accommodate post-quantum signatures without losing speed. Amid advanced AI models and quantum breakthroughs, blockchains now face double security threats. 

Google has set an internal post-quantum deadline of 2029. Some blockchains like Tron and Starknet are at advanced stages to meet the deadline. Others, such as Quantus, Tezos, and Algorand, are quantum-ready, but Bitcoin and Ethereum are yet to agree on the PQ signatures to use.      

For his part, Vibhu Norby, Solana Chief Product Officer, said, 

Solana is ready for quantum & whatever comes next with AI. Anza’s cryptography team is world class

Similarly, Jacob Creech also hailed the Quantumglow plan, adding that it’s “simple and has no loss in speed.” 

Solana quantum push: What’s at risk?

As mentioned earlier, signatures or approvals at the validator/consensus level and app or wallet transfers are secured by classical cryptography. Similarly, the risks extend to crypto custody and bridge systems. 

This makes the entire blockchain tech stack that relies on classical signatures at risk from advanced AI models or quantum computers. Currently, $2.7 trillion, or 99.7% of the crypto market, is still vulnerable. 

In fact, even Solana is still vulnerable and has an ‘F’ rating because it currently does not use post-quantum signatures across its entire stack, including transactions, P2P transfers, and the consensus layer. 

Final Summary

  • Solana announced Quantumglow to make the chain quantum-proof, but no timeline was shared.
  • The L1 currently has an ‘F’ rating in quantum readiness but still leads Ethereum in planned migration.

data.title: Zcash falls 7.34% as its rebound stalls—Can $1,200 hold?
data.description:
Zcash [ZEC] lost 7.34% on October 22, interrupting a recovery that saw it briefly go above the $1,300 price area. At the time of this writing, it was near the $1,225 price level, slightly above the day’s opening level.

The setback puts the $1,200 price area back in focus as futures numbers also decline. All this is coming as developers release software for the planned network upgrade in November, giving holders another development to watch apart from the daily swings.

A setback after a sharp recovery

ZEC had climbed from about $1,100 toward $1,350 before Thursday’s decline of over 7% erased most of that gain.

But despite the loss, the daily chart shows some ground remains below the price. ZEC held above its 50-day price average near the $1,193 price level, while its longer-term averages was considerably lower.

That leaves $1,190–$1,200 as the immediate test for it. If it holds this area, part of the recovery will be preserved. But if it continues to trade below it, it could go down to its recent lows around the $1,100 price area.

Buyers also face a nearby obstacle. Friday’s rise reached around $1,259 before easing, making the $1,240–$1,260 price area the first area to recover and hold. Beyond that, the latest rebound’s peak around the $1,320–$1,360 price area remains a harder challenge.

Futures exposure retreats alongside the price

CoinGlass’s open interest chart shows the dollar value of outstanding ZEC futures contracts falling after a recent jump toward $3 billion.

Its decline can show positions closing, but falling ZEC prices also reduce their dollar value.

November’s upgrade moves a step closer

The Zcash Foundation released Zebra 7.0.0 on October 22, providing stable software support for the forthcoming NU7 upgrade.

Activation is set for block 3,543,405, which is expected to be around November 5. The upgrade targets a reduction in block times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, which will shorten the expected wait for a first transaction confirmation.

Daily ZEC issuance and the 21 million supply cap remain unchanged.

Final Summary

  • Zcash steadied near $1,225 after Thursday’s 7.34% loss, leaving $1,200 as an immediate test.
  • NU7 software is available ahead of expected November activation, while futures exposure has contracted.

data.title: CoinDCX faces fresh scrutiny over $16M crypto transfers – What happened?
data.description:
Another day, another exploit, and this time CoinDCX, one of the biggest cryptocurrency exchanges in India, is facing scrutiny after suspicious movements involving wallets previously linked to the exchange. According to Darcy (an on-chain investigator), CoinDCX was linked to a suspected $16 million security incident.

On the 21st of October, 2026, approximately 15.99 million USDT and 5,784 TRX were transferred from addresses previously associated with CoinDCX to a single TRON wallet.

In this, the largest transaction involved 15.82 million USDT, after which the funds were split and routed to deposit addresses linked to Binance, OKX, and Gate.

CoinDCX’s co-founder stirs the pot

However, things became heated when CoinDCX co-founder Sumit Gupta denied that the exchange’s active wallets had been compromised. He described the transactions as hackers reusing compromised addresses from the previous incident.

Gupta said,

Thanks for highlighting but this is incorrect and CoinDCX wallets are not breached. Pls don’t spread rumours.

Gupta added,

We have checked all the present CoinDCX central and user addresses. None of them have sent money to these old addresses.

Additionally, co-founder Gupta issued an updated statement explaining that the flagged addresses, including the TQKJQ wallet, had been ‘deprecated’ following the July 2025 exploit.

CoinDCX said it had absorbed the operational losses and credited all affected users. They also noted that their customer assets remained protected in segregated cold storage.

However, blockchain investigator ZachXBT challenged this explanation and presented on-chain evidence for the same.

ZachXBT calls CoinDCX founders ‘clowns’

According to ZachXBT, the address remained active with a liquidity provider, regularly processed user deposits, and interacted with a current CoinDCX hot wallet as recently as April and May 2026.

Remarking on the same, the pseudonymous blockchain investigator added,

Withdraw all funds from CoinDCX if you value your assets. Its co-founders are clowns running a circus.

Naturally, these findings have raised questions on whether the addresses should genuinely be considered inactive. They have also sparked concerns over whether approximately $15.8 million in assets had actually gone missing.

What’s more to this?

Needless to say, this isn’t the first time CoinDCX has been attacked. Back in July 2025, the crypto exchange had already suffered a $44 million hack.

Interestingly, while this CoinDCX exploit was making headlines, SunCrypto, another crypto exchange of India, reported server-side technical issues that have temporarily made its app unavailable.

Now, while its team is working to restore services as soon as possible, the exchange assured users that their funds remain safe and secure.

Final Summary

  • Darcy alleged that CoinDCX was suspected of the transfer of approximately 15.99 million USDT and 5,784 TRX.
  • But CoinDCX co-founder Sumit Gupta rejected claims of the exchange’s active wallets being compromised.

data.title: Blockchain Association urges Congress to ease crypto tax rules for 67M holders
data.description:
In a recent development, the Blockchain Association (BA) has urged the U.S. Congress to introduce clearer and fairer tax rules for cryptocurrencies. They believe that existing regulations create uncertainty and unnecessary compliance burdens for the 67 million Americans who hold and use digital assets.

Therefore, in a letter dated the 22nd of October, 2026, addressed to Senate and House leaders, the industry group outlined its Digital Asset Tax Principles. In fact, they even called for bipartisan legislation that reflects how digital assets function today.

Besides this, the BA also launched TaxClarityforAmerica.com to encourage Americans to contact their elected representatives and support the proposed reforms.

What is the motive behind this?

With this move, the association is seeking a meaningful ‘de minimis’ exemption to simplify taxes on small crypto transactions and cash-like tax treatment for stablecoins. This in turn is intended to reduce reporting requirements potentially.

At the same time, the BA also proposed taxing mining and staking rewards when they are sold or disposed of, rather than when users initially receive them. This is a step that would prevent tax liabilities on rewards that have not been converted into cash.

Additionally, it wants broker reporting requirements to apply only to intermediaries that have custody or control of customer assets. This excludes non-custodial developers and infrastructure providers to protect privacy.

Key recommendation by the Blockchain Association

Another key proposal is to prevent taxes from being triggered when users transfer digital assets between their own wallets, interact with smart contracts, or move assets across blockchains. However, this comes with a condition that their underlying economic ownership remains unchanged.

The association also supports extending wash-sale rules to crypto to prevent investors from claiming artificial losses while ensuring that everyday transactions are not unfairly penalized.

That said, other recommendations include allowing crypto investments in retirement accounts, clarifying staking rules for trusts and investment vehicles. Additionally, permitting mark-to-market accounting for eligible digital assets, simplifying charitable donations of regularly traded cryptocurrencies. It also proposes recognizing blockchain development as eligible research and development activity for tax credits.

The group further advocates a statutory safe harbor for foreign investors trading digital assets on U.S. exchanges. Here, they argue that clearer tax rules could attract liquidity, encourage businesses to remain in the U.S, and prevent innovation from moving offshore.

The unsaid caveat

However, it is important to note that these proposals have not yet been enacted into law.  

Instead, they just represent the Blockchain Association’s recommendations to Congress, and any changes would require legislative action before taking effect.

Still, Coinbase CPO applauded this move when he noted, 

Notably, this coincided with the Blockchain Association (BA) submitting a comment letter to the U.S. Treasury on proposed GENIUS Act regulations, while warning against excessive compliance burdens on crypto firms, exchanges, and DeFi platforms.

Interestingly, all of this follows the U.S. CFTC, led by Chairman Michael Selig, plans to bring more of the crypto market under a unified federal framework after the CLARITY Act failed to advance in September.

Final Summary

  • Blockchain Association outlined its Digital Asset Tax Principles and called for bipartisan legislation. 
  • All the suggestions given by BA are just recommendations to Congress and are not yet accounted for as law.

data.title: Bitcoin Open Interest jumps 8% – Why BTC price faces liquidation risks
data.description:
Bitcoin’s [BTC] latest recovery appears increasingly dependent on leveraged Futures buying rather than Spot demand alone. Futures Open Interest (OI) grew 8.04% to $27.12 billion within 24 hours. Despite that, BTC retraced to below $82,000 at press time.

This rise suggests traders are opening new positions to capture further gains, adding momentum to the recovery. However, as seen in prior rallies in August and September, these large increases in OI were followed by sharp declines in price and multiple sell alerts.

Increases in leverage therefore can provide significant impetus to an increase in price. However, they can also make a trader very susceptible to being forced into liquidation at a loss. Since Futures OI is trending back up after a fall-off in October.

Sustained buying could support further gains. Still, if investor sentiment begins to deteriorate, then there could be a cascade of forced liquidations and a larger drop in price.

Altcoins overtake Bitcoin in OI

The dominance of Bitcoin derivatives has weakened significantly as traders continue to use leverage to bet on altcoins. Historically, Bitcoin has held over 90% of all OI. In contrast, currently it accounts for less than half, 42.6%, against altcoins’ 57.4%.

This reversal accelerated from 2022, when the percentage of Bitcoin’s leveraged contracts plummeted and the use of altcoin contracts became much more widespread among large exchange users.

As such, this indicates that there is an opportunity for investment in altcoins beyond Bitcoin. However, this may also mean that the potential for greater losses due to a rapid decline in price for the same altcoins may be dispersed throughout a wider range of assets.

Bitcoin leverage faces liquidation risks

Growing leverage in both Bitcoin and altcoins raises an important issue. Will the leverage currently available in the marketplace be enough to sustain itself?

Although altcoins now represent approximately 57.4% of all OI, it is still too early to determine whether Bitcoin’s current positioning represents an indication. The market will be able to sustain the high level of leverage it is experiencing.

Aggregated Futures OI levels range from $30 billion to $53 billion. Funding Rates have remained steady around +0.004%. As such, there does not appear to be widespread long-side crowding.

Therefore, spot demand will be needed to provide additional support for BTC’s continued growth and will not rely solely on leverage.

Final Summary

data.title: Uniswap expands trading routes, bringing outside swaps into UNI burns
data.description:
Uniswap launched a feature called Aggregator Hooks on October 22 that lets its trading system access funds available on other decentralized exchanges.

The change also increases the trading activity that contributes to UNI burns. Uniswap says swaps routed through these outside sources pay protocol fees, which means their use will lead to the removal of UNI tokens from circulation.

More places to find a trade

When someone exchanges one token for another, the funds needed to complete that trade can sit across different platforms.

This new feature allows Uniswap to check connected outside sources with its own trading pools. Its system compares quotes and builds a route to allow the swap to be completed.

For regular users, the change happens behind the scenes. The web app includes those sources automatically, and the trade settles in one transaction without an additional approval step required from the user, according to the announcement seen from Uniswap.

This expands the options available to its trading system.

How outside trades connect to UNI

The fee connection gives UNI holders another reason to watch the adoption of the feature.

This is because trades using the connected sources pay Uniswap protocol fees that contribute to token burns. 

What the launch then does is it adds another activity that can support those burns. But how much it adds will depend on the trading it sees through these new routes.

Uniswap’s post did not provide any figures for additional fees that have been collected or UNI burnt since launch. The effect on supply remains to be seen as usage develops.

A substantial trading business already exists

According to the DefiLlama data reviewed by AMBCrypto, there was about $69.4 billion in trading volume over 30 days. It also recorded around $8.4 million in protocol revenue during that period.

Those figures show the extent of the current Uniswap activity. What they mostly show is trading before the October 22 launch, which means that what the new feature contributes cannot be really calculated yet.

For now, the confirmed development is broader access to trading sources and a fee connection to UNI burns. Subsequent usage and revenue data will help to see how much the expansion adds.

Final Summary

  • Uniswap now automatically includes outside trading sources across supported networks.
  • These fees contribute to UNI burns, but the additional impact is not known yet.
